laura: quick bring-up notes for cheetah-compact (256-d) quant sweep — posting scatter/nn diffs for review :mag_right:

laura: summary (holdout 30k stratified head/longtail): recall@1/5/10 float32 0.689 / 0.841 / 0.903  | int8 0.674 / 0.826 / 0.895  | int6 0.632 / 0.788 / 0.853
laura: avg cosine shift median (f32->quant): int8 0.009, int6 0.035; 99th pctile int6 ~0.18 (longtail heavy)

devin: those drops look larger than we saw on the 512-d family. did you change pooling?

laura: same pooling (mean pooling + l2 postnorm). difference is dim reduction from 512->256 and aggressive 6-bit per-channel clamp for int6. also tried per-tensor symmetric for int6 as a quick baseline.

priya: any cluster-level metrics? silhouette or cluster purity?

laura: silhouette (cosine) float32 0.198 -> int8 0.184 -> int6 0.122. cluster purity (kmeans 200 clusters) dropped ~6% int6 vs f32. UMAP snapshots in artifacts show small topical niches merging in int6.

matt: can you link the NN-diff sample? I want to eyeball what "flipped" looks like for product queries.

laura: uploaded nn_diff.tsv + examples.jsonl to s3://redwood-evals/cheetah-compact/1747755555/ . small sample pasted below for quick look:
```
# query_id	f32_nn	int6_nn	query_text
q931	DOC_4421	DOC_7712	"how to rotate an image in python"
q1420	DOC_883	DOC_883	"refund policy for subscription"
q2400	DOC_1203	DOC_9931	"french to english legal translation"
```

laura: note q931 is longtail tutorial query 1; int6 replaced a closer textual match with a more generic tutorial (loss of exact match). q2400 is cross-lingual flip (embedding collapsed language-specific signal in int6).

devin: cross-lingual flips are worrying. did you try per-output-channel scaling or bias-correction?

laura: ran a 5-point minmax clip sweep + asymmetric per-channel quant for int6 on 5k calibration samples. results: recall@10 improved from 0.853 -> 0.872, median cosine shift down from 0.035 -> 0.022. but 99th pctile still high (~0.11).

priya: promising. what about fine-tune-aware PTQ (bias correction) on a tiny subset?

laura: scheduled a 1% FT-aware bias-correct run overnight. also trying output-channel rescale (per-row) that helped centroids before.

matt: for rollout thinking: maybe index-time re-embed for cold store (cheap) and keep int8 for online recall. but we need to check NN-diff recall loss vs cost-win.

laura: agree. my proposal: if FT-aware int6 can get recall@1 within 2% absolute of int8 and keep 95th pctile cosine shift <0.08 then we can consider cold-index use. otherwise stick to int8 for production.

eval-bot: CI: emb-eval job 1747755555 completed  artifacts: recall_table.csv, nn_diff.tsv, umap_longtail.png uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/cheetah-compact/1747755555/ :white_check_mark:

devin: can you also dump nearest neighbors for the top 500 head queries? want to confirm head stability (we expect head to be robust).

laura: will do. adding head-500 dump to the artifacts, re-run scheduled. ETA EOD local timezone.

priya: once NN diffs are in, I'll spot-check 50 longtail queries (incl cross-lingual). I'll annotate flips as "acceptable" vs "regression" and report counts.

laura: thanks all 1 cc @devin @priya @matt — will post follow-ups in this thread when sweeps complete.
